summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest UK/EU movers.

• 6 upside misses — BNZL.L +5%, RWE.DE +4%, SSE.L +4%, HWDN.L +3%, TSCO.L +3%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (AKZA.AS -17%, PRX.AS -6%, G24.DE -5%, ADYEN.AS -5%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: AKZA.AS (-17.22%) — Nippon Paint/Sherwin-Williams formally withdrew their €73/share (€12.5B) cash takeover bid on Jun 4 after Akzo Nobel's board rejected it as undervaluing the company; collapse of the bid premium drove the ~17% drop. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe. AKZA.AS was in a live merger-arb situation (competing €73 cash bid vs. Axalta all-stock deal); its price was dominated by takeover-premium dynamics, not momentum or mean-reversion signals. The gap was a discrete pre-market event unreachable by any technical filter.

top_movers.catalyst: RWE formally announced completion of its full €1.5B share buyback program (9.5M shares retired) on June 3 after close, removing supply overhang and reinforcing capital discipline alongside confirmed FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance of €2.20–2.90.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — RWE is a DAX-listed large-cap European utility (~€35B mkt cap) typically screened out by bots scoped to UK-only or mid-cap names. The trigger was a capital-allocation event (buyback completion press release) where pre-announcement positioning beats any post-open technical signal
top_movers.suggestion: Add a corporate-action news filter for DAX/EURO STOXX utilities: when a buyback-completion RNS/ad-hoc is filed and the name sits within 8% of its 4-week low, release it into the news-reactive strategy's eligible universe within the first 30 minutes of Xetra open.

top_movers.catalyst: FY26 preliminary results (28 May) showed EPS 153.5p at guidance upper end with +7% dividend hike to 68.7p; confirmed by €1.3bn hybrid capital raise (2 Jun) priced 8× oversubscribed, validating the fully-funded £33bn five-year capex plan.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe; SSE.L is a FTSE 100 large-cap regulated utility (~£28bn mkt cap) likely excluded by sector and size filters. The move was a multi-day post-results drift — too slow and event-driven for momentum or mean-reversion intraday signals to trigger entry.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a post-results news-reactive gate for FTSE 100 regulated utilities: enter within 3 sessions of preliminary results where dividend growth ≥5% and EPS meets/beats guidance upper bound, gated by a ≥1% day-1 gap-up confirmation to avoid false positives.

top_movers.catalyst: Howden Joinery announced acquisition of online kitchen retailer DIY Kitchens for £390m (announced after close 3 Jun); market digested the bolt-on M&A — 17% pa revenue growth, 27% EBIT margins — on 4 Jun open.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — HWDN.L is a FTSE 100 home-improvement supplier not covered by current sector/cap filters. Move was M&A-driven from a prior-close announcement; capturing it required overnight positioning before the gap printed at open.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an M&A-release gate: if a FTSE 100/250 name announces a strategic acquisition after close and gaps ≥+2% at open, inject it into the news-reactive strategy's candidate list within 15 min of open for follow-through momentum entry.

top_movers.catalyst: Ongoing £750m share buyback (£231m completed since 22 Apr) provided steady price floor; a UK retail-sales beat and analyst Buy / £5.15 target reiteration likely triggered a 3% technical snap-back from a 12% YTD drawdown.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. TSCO.L is a ~£28B large-cap defensive grocer; its move was mean-reversion off a multi-month drawdown rather than a momentum break-out, and with shares below the 20/50/200-day MAs pre-move most momentum and gap-up filters would have scored it neutral or negative.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a 'buyback-accelerator' scan to the UK large-cap universe: names with an active buyback consuming ≥0.5% of float per month AND price ≥5% below the 52-week high qualify for a mean-reversion entry — this would have surfaced TSCO.L before the snap-back.

top_movers.catalyst: SBRY traded ex-dividend 4 Jun 2026 for a 9.6p final dividend (~3.2% yield); the reported +2.80% close-to-close gain is a total-return (dividend-adjusted) artefact — raw shares were flagged among FTSE 100 index-drag leaders on the day.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. SBRY is a FTSE 100 large-cap UK consumer staples stock (~£7bn mkt cap); the apparent 'gain' is an ex-dividend total-return artefact, not a price-momentum or mean-reversion signal any technical strategy would target.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a pre/on-ex-div suppression flag: exclude names from the daily top-gainers watchlist on ex-dividend date ±1 session when dividend yield ≥1.5%, preventing total-return dividend adjustments from inflating the signal list with non-actionable entries.

top_movers.catalyst: Nippon Paint/Sherwin-Williams formally withdrew their €73/share (€12.5B) cash takeover bid on Jun 4 after Akzo Nobel's board rejected it as undervaluing the company; collapse of the bid premium drove the ~17% drop.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. AKZA.AS was in a live merger-arb situation (competing €73 cash bid vs. Axalta all-stock deal); its price was dominated by takeover-premium dynamics, not momentum or mean-reversion signals. The gap was a discrete pre-market event unreachable by any technical filter.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a merger-arb quarantine flag: names with an announced acquisition bid should be excluded from momentum/mean-reversion universes until the deal closes or fully lapses — the bid-premium component makes all technical entries unreliable.

top_movers.catalyst: Prosus sold 5% Delivery Hero stake to Aspex Management for €335M (€22/share), second disposal in weeks; investors read accelerating portfolio liquidation as structural NAV negative.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. PRX.AS is a ~€40B Amsterdam tech-holding co. whose price is driven by portfolio corporate actions; no momentum or mean-reversion signal precedes a surprise stake-disposal RNS.
top_movers.suggestion: Add Amsterdam large-cap holding companies (mkt cap ≥€10B) to a news-reactive universe; gate entry on RNS stake-disposal filings ≥€200M, triggering directional position within 30 min of publish.

top_movers.catalyst: Scout24 pre-filed AGM buyback blackout (no repurchases Jun 5–17), removing the €250M programme's mechanical bid the day before suspension began; market sold off as the price-support floor was pulled.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe (MDAX German PropTech portal). Catalyst was a pre-filed corporate-action disclosure (AGM buyback blackout), not earnings or momentum, so news-reactive and technical filters had no pre-move signal to act on.
top_movers.suggestion: Add buyback-blackout events to the corporate-calendar feed: flag names entering a disclosed MAR suspension window (≥€50M) within 2 trading days as short candidates — this would have caught the Jun 4 pre-AGM selloff.

top_movers.catalyst: CFO Ethan Tandowsky announced surprise departure effective August 2026, unsettling investors already digesting a Q1 EPS miss (€17.66 vs €17.94 est) and a guidance range reset to 20-22% growth.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — ADYEN.AS is a large-cap Euronext Amsterdam fintech (~€26.75B mkt cap) not covered by current strategy universes. Even if added, the move was triggered by a surprise executive departure with no pre-market technical footprint, making it uncatchable by momentum or mean-reversion si
top_movers.suggestion: Add top-20 AEX large-caps (including ADYEN.AS) to a news-reactive strategy universe; gate entries on RNS/press-release C-suite departure events where stock gaps >3% from prior close within 45 minutes of open.
